Plain English meaning: All answers converted to a 0-100 scale. 100 means every student strongly agreed; 50 is neutral; 0 means every student strongly disagreed.
Add up all students' scores for a topic and divide by how many students answered.
A word for the score: 80+ Very good, 60-79 Good, 40-59 Needs work, below 40 Poor.
The middle half of students fall in this range. A quarter scored lower, a quarter scored higher.
Whether students gave similar answers or very different ones. Wide disagreement means one average hides two different experiences.
The difference in average score between two groups, in points out of 100.
Whether the gap is big enough that it is unlikely to be a fluke of who happened to answer. 'No' means treat the two groups as equal.
How meaningful the gap is in practice. A gap can be real but still tiny and unimportant.
Whether two topics rise and fall together across students.
Whether the questions grouped under one topic actually measure the same thing. Above 0.70 is the accepted standard.
How many people gave a usable answer. Small numbers mean less reliable results.
